terms.gloss: intervene, step in between; of a tribune, veto
evidence: Cic. Leg. 3.8: nisi mihi levissimus tribūnus plēbis intercessisset (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally to come or be between; so to intervene for or against someone, and in Roman politics to veto a measure. The noun is intercessiō (veto; intervention).

evidence: Cic. Fam. 10.27.2: sī tē in istam pācificātiōnem nōn interpōnis (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Q. fr. 3.4.5: mē nihil interpōnō
terms.comment: To put oneself into a matter, for good or ill; mē nihil interpōnō is “I’m staying out of it”.
Someone’s arrival or stepping in; also of things that come between (interventū noctis, Caes. BG 3.15).

phrases.english: The brothers are squabbling; I don’t want to get involved.

sources: Lewis & Short: intercedo · Lewis & Short: interpono · Lewis & Short: interventus
